decisionReasons: Counterfactual do-no-harm admission, alternate-safe-policy constraints, minimum-disruption control, runtime fallback and coalition externality accounting already cover the proposed control mechanism. The remaining novelty is only a V2X-membership-conditioned outsider estimand.
The original max-over-outsiders endpoint cannot justify an actor-wise non-regression claim and can hide burden transfer between outsiders.

A valid causal contrast requires a pre-message full-state snapshot, complete reactive closed-loop twins, treatment-invariant outsider membership, nested policy construction and an independent rollout evaluator.

Neither pinned MDrive nor pinned Flow supplies a complete public cooperative-message or masked-policy path with a responsive outsider and episode-level outcomes. Connecting them requires a new response adapter whose semantics would define the measured effect.
Because one independent gate is reject and the other two require material reframing, the candidate cannot enter score-bearing blind review.
claimBoundary: The closure rejects this candidate under the currently verified public assets. It does not claim that V2X cooperation can never impose nonparticipant externalities.
reopenOnlyIf: A fixed public stack exposes cooperative and message-masked branches from the same pre-treatment state, with response-capable nonparticipants and complete episode traces.
The public path runs without a newly authored response model defining the target effect.
The contribution is explicitly limited to a membership-conditioned empirical estimand unless a mechanism beyond existing do-no-harm and minimum-disruption priors is proven.
Actor-wise or lexicographically ordered outsider burden replaces the invalid max-only non-regression claim.
Nested policy construction and independent closed-loop evaluation are executable within the declared two-week budget.
